tools.name: analyze_market
tools.title: Analyzing the market
tools.description: Bring Liquid's powerful market intelligence into the conversation: real-time prices, funding, and proprietary positioning insights in one place. PRIMARY TOOL for any question about a specific tradeable asset on Liquid. Use this whenever the user asks about an asset's price, outlook, positioning, sentiment, what an asset is doing, how traders are positioned, or wants analysis on a particular market. Liquid covers equities (TSLA, AAPL, NVDA), commodities (GOLD, SILVER, CL for WTI crude, BRENT for Brent crude), indices (SP500), crypto (BTC, ETH, SOL), and more. If the result requires an asset choice, ask the user which candidate they mean and retry with its exact symbol. Returns real-time Liquid price, funding, OI, and positioning data, including the smart-money (profitable traders) vs losing-crowd long/short split when available. Do NOT use search_markets when the user asks about a specific known asset — use analyze_market instead. After presenting the analysis, offer in your own reply to turn it into a trade (a paper trade when paper trading is active; otherwise mention they can paper trade risk-free with $10k simulated funds, or deposit and trade for real). Do NOT call suggest_trade until the user says yes.

tools.name: get_transaction_history
tools.title: Loading transaction history
tools.description: Bring the user's trading and money movement into one clear, newest-first activity timeline: trade fills, deposits, withdrawals, sends/receives, account transfers, and prediction-market trades with human-readable market names. Use when the user asks for their transactions, activity, trade history, past trades, deposit/withdrawal history, or 'what have I done recently'. Do NOT confuse with get_portfolio (current balances and open positions) or view_open_orders (resting orders) — this shows PAST activity. The response's paperMode flag applies only to Trade rows: while paper trading is active they are simulated fills, never real trades, but Deposit/Withdraw/Send/Receive/Transfer rows are always the user's real wallet activity and are never simulated — do not describe them as paper trades. Use the type filter to narrow to just trades, transfers, or prediction activity. Coverage is RECENT history, not all-time: each source contributes its most recent window (Liquid returns roughly the ~2000 most recent trade fills and ledger updates; prediction activity is the order history the backend returns), `total` counts rows in that fetched snapshot, and `offset` pages within it — not through older, unfetched history.

limit.description: Maximum rows to return after merging all sources. Defaults to 10, max 100.

offset.description: Rows to skip after merging and sorting (newest-first) — use offset=limit*N to page. Pages within the fetched recent-history snapshot only (each source's most recent window), never into older history. Applied before limit. Defaults to 0.

type.description: Filter: 'trades' for fills only, 'transfers' for deposits/withdrawals/sends/receives, 'predictions' for prediction-market activity, 'all' for everything. Defaults to all.

skipCache.description: Internal: bypass the 5s history caches. Used by the transaction-list widget on mount and manual refresh so the user always sees up-to-the-second data.

tools.name: plan_portfolio
tools.title: Planning your portfolio
tools.description: Turn market research and personal preferences into a cohesive multi-trade portfolio plan in one shot. Use this when the user asks for a 'portfolio', 'plan', 'how should I deploy $X', 'suggest a few trades', or any multi-position allocation question — instead of suggesting trades one at a time. PREREQUISITE: BEFORE calling this tool, you MUST collect the user's preferences using the client's built-in interactive question widget (the one rendered for AskUserQuestion / structured Q&A). NEVER ask the questions as a numbered prose list in chat — always use the native question UI. Required answers: (1) risk tolerance (conservative | moderate | aggressive), (2) time horizon (intraday | swing_week | position_long_term), (3) assetClasses as an array of one or more selected asset class strings from crypto, equities, commodities, indices, fx. Do NOT ask about balance — this tool fetches the user's available_balance from their portfolio and assumes they want to deploy all of it. Once you have the three answers, call this tool. It fetches the account balance + news + market-wide positioning + top-trader cohort + unusual volume in parallel (plus upcoming earnings when equities are selected) and returns a research bundle plus sizing rules and synthesis instructions. AFTER this tool returns, you must (a) write a 2–3 sentence thesis, (b) call suggest_trades_batch ONCE with that thesis plus all proposed legs as a basket, then (c) write a 1–2 sentence risk wrap. Do NOT call suggest_trade per-leg — always use suggest_trades_batch for portfolio plans. Do NOT write the trade plan in prose or a markdown table.

tools.name: suggest_order
tools.title: Suggesting a paper order
tools.description: Prepare a paper-only order review link in Liquid after checking market and account context. This tool never places an order and cannot choose live mode. Paper trading mode must already be active for your wallet. Review the prefilled order in Liquid and confirm paper mode before placing it. Size is notional USD; sizeBasis preserves the user’s intended collateral or notional when leverage changes.

asset.description: Liquid asset identifier. Examples: BTC, ETH, GOLD.

limitPrice.description: Limit price (required if orderType is limit)

timeInForce.description: Time-in-force for limit orders: 'gtc' rests on the book until filled or cancelled (default), 'ioc' fills whatever is immediately available and cancels the remainder, 'alo' is post-only / add-liquidity-only (rejected instead of taking liquidity). Ignored for market orders.

size.description: Order size as a USD notional dollar amount (collateral × leverage) — NOT a quantity of coins/contracts. E.g. 250 means $250 of exposure, not 250 units. Minimum $10 collateral × leverage. Always pass this as notional at your requested leverage, even when sizeBasis is 'margin' (e.g. $300 margin at 3x leverage is size=900, not size=300) — sizeBasis never converts this value for you. (e.g. $50 at 5x, $100 at 10x).

sizeBasis.description: `size` must already be the notional dollar amount computed at requestedLeverage regardless of this field — sizeBasis does NOT convert a margin/collateral number into notional for you (compute notional yourself as margin × requestedLeverage before calling). This only controls what gets preserved if the venue ends up using a different leverage than requestedLeverage (e.g. inheriting an existing position's leverage, or a leverage cap): 'notional' keeps size's dollar exposure fixed and recomputes margin; 'margin' keeps the margin implied by size/requestedLeverage fixed and recomputes notional at the new leverage. Defaults to margin for compatibility with the deployed links distribution.

user_intent.description: One-sentence paraphrase of the user's request that led to this tool call. Include when you have conversational context.

order.description: Order details or order proposal payload.

tools.name: view_open_orders
tools.title: Viewing open orders
tools.description: List the user's currently open orders — includes resting limit orders and position-level trigger orders (TP/SL). Use when the user asks about pending orders, working orders, resting limits, or current TP/SL levels. Do NOT confuse with get_portfolio — this shows ORDERS (pending/resting), not POSITIONS (active holdings). Returns text (no widget) with order id, symbol, side, kind (limit/tp/sl/trigger), size, price or trigger, and flags, followed by a protection-coverage readback for every position with a live TP/SL trigger (a fixed-size leg can stop covering the full position after an add, or after a partial close). The order id can be passed to cancel_order to cancel. Perpetual orders only — HIP-4 prediction-market orders are excluded (they would otherwise render as an unresolvable bare id with a probability shown as a dollar price); use view_prediction_orders for those.
